title: Chartwise and topological morphism properties of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$. Use the field-valued point classes, their atlas topology and point images of [def-a1-space-point-topology], the induced point map and quasi-compactness of [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli], and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For a property $P$ of scheme morphisms, its chart test for $f$ means that for every pair of $S$-schemes $U,V$, every representable etale maps $a:h_U\to X$, $b:h_V\to Y$, and every $S$-morphism $h:U\to V$ with $f a=b h$, the scheme morphism $h$ has $P$. Define flatness and local finite presentation of $f$ by this chart test with the scheme properties [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Define separatedness by requiring its diagonal to be representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Define finite type by quasi-compactness and the chart test for locally finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Define universal closedness by requiring $|X\times_Y Y'|\to |Y'|$ to be closed for every algebraic-space morphism $Y'\to Y$. Proper means separated, finite type and universally closed, in agreement with the scheme convention [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Finally, universally open means that $|X\times_Y Y'|\to |Y'|$ is open for every algebraic-space morphism $Y'\to Y$.
